procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 14.10.2009 of the High Court of M.P. at Jabalpur in CRLA No. 1949 of 2007, which confirmed the appellant’s conviction under Section 353 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentence of six months simple imprisonment and fine of Rs. 1,000/-.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellant, aggrieved by the Special Judge's decision, appealed to the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur in Criminal Appeal No. 1949 of 2007. The High Court dismissed the appeal, confirming the conviction and sentence.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant, still aggrieved, appealed to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal.

decision.conviction_status: The appellant would stand acquitted for the offence under Section 353 of the IPC. The Conviction under Section 353 of the IPC... are set aside.
decision.sentence_status: The sentence imposed are set aside.
directions: The bail bonds shall stand discharged.

issue.issue_text: Whether the conviction of the appellant under s.353 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) can be sustained without proving assault and use of criminal force.

facts: The appellant was charged under Section 353 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) following a trap proceeding related to a bribery allegation.
The specific allegation was that the appellant attacked or used criminal force on the members of the trap team to obstruct them from performing their public duty.
The appellant was convicted by a Special Judge, and the conviction was upheld by the High Court.
The appeal before the Supreme Court was solely concerned with the conviction under Section 353 IPC.
law: The Court held that the use of 'criminal force' or 'assault' are necessary and essential ingredients to constitute an offence under Section 353 of the IPC.
It defined 'criminal force' as per Section 350 IPC, which requires the use of force on a person without their consent in order to commit an offence.
It defined 'assault' as per Section 351 IPC, which involves making a gesture or preparation that causes a person to apprehend the imminent use of criminal force.
application: The Court examined the oral and medical evidence on record to determine if the appellant had used criminal force or committed an assault.
Upon reviewing the evidence, the Court found that the prosecution was unable to establish that the appellant had actually assaulted or used criminal force against the trap party.
The Court concluded that none of the essential ingredients required to maintain a conviction under Section 353 of the IPC had been proven by the prosecution.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that since the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of assault or the use of criminal force, the conviction of the appellant under Section 353 of the IPC could not be sustained. Consequently, the Court set aside the conviction and acquitted the appellant of the charge.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the conviction of the appellant under s.353 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) can be sustained without proving assault and use of criminal force.
appellant_arguments: The conviction under Section 353 of the IPC was not justified.

The evidence provided by prosecution witnesses (PW-1 Babulal Ahirwar, PW-4 O.P. Tiwari, PW-8 N.K. Parihar, PW-9 Niranjan Singh, and PW-13 Dr. H.L. Bhuria) does not make out a case for conviction under Section 353 of the IPC.
None of the ingredients required to maintain a conviction under Section 353 of the IPC have been established.
The appellant's wife was acquitted on the same evidence.
respondent_arguments: No case for interference with the concurrent conviction by the lower courts is made out.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: To constitute an offence under Section 353 of the IPC, a person must assault or use criminal force against a public servant under one of three conditions: (a) while the public servant is executing their duty, (b) with the intent to prevent or deter the public servant from discharging their duty, or (c) as a consequence of something the public servant has done or attempted to do in the lawful discharge of their duty.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: Upon a perusal of the evidence on record concerning the charge under Section 353 of the IPC, the court found that none of the essential ingredients required to convict a person under that section were attracted.
legal_tests_applied: The ingredients for an offence under Section 353 of the IPC, which requires that a person "assaults or uses criminal force to any person being a public servant in the execution of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person from discharging his duty as such public servant, or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by such person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant".
